sections.heading: C — Sharing the Road (Section 14)
sections.markdown:
## C — Sharing the Road (Section 14)

FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A01
Utah treats pedestrians, highway workers, animal riders, farm gear without a cab, boards, skates, cycles, scooters, motorcycles and wheelchairs as vulnerable highway users [A01].
Why it matters: sets who gets extra protection in later passing rules.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A01
Deliberately distracting or forcing a vulnerable user off the road can bring a citation, record entry and points [A01].
Why it matters: harassment toward walkers and riders is scored as a violation.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A01
Bicycles on the road count as vehicles with the same rights and duties as cars [A01].
Why it matters: frames every bike right-of-way decision.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A01
Drivers yield to bikes at crossings and keep off marked bike lanes except to enter a drive, obey police or handle an emergency [A01].
Why it matters: lane intrusion is a common trap.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A02
When passing any bicyclist or vulnerable user, Utah requires at least three feet of clearance [A02].
Why it matters: exact distance is highly testable.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A02
Drivers dim headlights within five hundred feet when near bikes at night and check before opening doors or backing [A02].
Why it matters: night and parking duties cluster together.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A02
A bike or moped may be passed only where sight lines allow, never blindly over a crest, curve, bridge, tunnel, crossing or within one hundred feet of them [A02].
Why it matters: no-pass zones mirror center-line rules.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A03
A bike brake must halt the machine within twenty-five feet from ten miles per hour, and night riders need white front, red rear and side visibility [A03].
Why it matters: equipment numbers are favorite exam details.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A04
On sirens or flashing emergency signals, drivers must pull at once to the right edge and halt until the vehicle passes [A04].
Why it matters: absolute yield tops every sharing question.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A04
Near a stopped roadside vehicle with hazards or amber lamps, slow down, give space and move a lane away when safe [A04].
Why it matters: move-over duty extends beyond police stops.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A04
Ignoring the move-over rule and being convicted means a four-hour classroom course within ninety days or a ninety-day suspension [A04].
Why it matters: penalty sequence is testable.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A05
No vehicle may exceed eight and one-half feet in width, while farm tractors may reach nine feet [A05].
Why it matters: width cap anchors size-regulation items.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A05
Road vehicles are capped at fourteen feet high, forty-five feet for a single unit, and sixty-five feet for most other combinations [A05].
Why it matters: three related caps are often confused.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-F14 | anchor: A05
Loads may project at most three feet ahead and six feet behind the body, with side overhang barred on the left and capped at six inches on the right [A05].
Why it matters: front, rear and side limits form one set.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-F15 | anchor: A06
Tractor-trailers favor the center lane on multilane roads, need far longer braking room and mislead judges of speed at crossings [A06].
Why it matters: explains why cars must not cut them off.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec14-F16 | anchor: A06
A car at fifty-five miles per hour stops in about one hundred thirty to one hundred forty feet, while a loaded rig can need over four hundred feet [A06].
Why it matters: contrast numbers show the cushion logic.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec14-F17 | anchor: A06
Long rigs swing left first for a right turn, so followers must wait for the maneuver to finish rather than squeeze past [A06].
Why it matters: turning path is a classic crash trap.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec14-F18 | anchor: A07
Truck blind areas reach about twenty feet ahead, along both flanks by the cab, and up to two hundred feet behind [A07].
Why it matters: exact zones define safe following and passing.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec14-F19 | anchor: A07
If a driver cannot see the trucker in the side mirror, the trucker cannot see that driver [A07].
Why it matters: one-line check replaces guessing about visibility.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec14-F20 | anchor: A07
Before returning after passing a large rig, the passer must see its full front in the rear-view mirror [A07].
Why it matters: prevents cut-off failures.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec14-F21 | anchor: A08
Mobility permits and pedestrian vehicles can use highways under stated conditions without standard registration or licensing [A08].
Why it matters: exception to normal credential rules.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec14-F22 | anchor: A08
Riders under fifteen need supervision or a certificate for motor-assisted scooters, and such scooters stay off fast or wide roads and posted no-board areas [A08].
Why it matters: age plus place limits combine in one rule.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec14-F23 | anchor: A09
Lane filtering past stopped traffic is allowed only on same-direction multilane roads or off-ramps capped at forty-five miles per hour, at fifteen miles per hour or less and only when safe [A09].
Why it matters: conditions separate legal filtering from banned splitting.
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec14-F24 | anchor: A09
A flashing bike or motorcycle signal may stay on by mistake, so drivers must not assume the rider will turn [A09].
Why it matters: signal trap appears in sharing scenarios.
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec14-F25 | anchor: A09
Drivers stay halted until a walker clears at least their half of the road, even without a marked crosswalk [A09].
Why it matters: half-road clearance is the stop-release test.
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec14-F26 | anchor: A09
Walkers with a guide dog or white cane get a full stop, and walkers without sidewalks use the left shoulder facing traffic [A09].
Why it matters: pairs helper and walker-placement duties.
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec14-F27 | anchor: A11
Slow vehicles show an orange-red triangle when below twenty-five miles per hour, and horses get quiet wide passes without horn or revving [A11].
Why it matters: links rural emblem and animal caution.
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec14-F28 | anchor: A12
Street-legal ATVs and UTVs use single-lane-each-way roads, keep to fifty miles per hour or less and hug the far right with reflector when the limit is higher [A12].
Why it matters: road-type plus speed plus position travel together.
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec14-F29 | anchor: A13
Stock no larger than manufacturer size with at least two thirty-seconds inch tread, plus lamps, signals, mirrors, horn, windshield or eye cover, and speedometer belong on street-legal all-terrain machines [A13].
Why it matters: equipment checklist is testable as a group.
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec14-F30 | anchor: A13
At crossings halt fifteen to fifty feet from the rail, never park within fifty feet, and never pass another same-direction car there [A13].
Why it matters: three distance and conduct rules share one spot.
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec14-F31 | anchor: A14
Flashing rail lights or bells mean full stop until they end, and gates must never be bypassed while moving or closed [A14].
Why it matters: absolute stop beats schedule pressure.
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec14-F32 | anchor: A15
Trains hold full priority over every road user, may come either way without schedule, and a loaded freight at fifty-five miles per hour can run over a mile to halt [A15].
Why it matters: weight and stopping truth motivate caution.
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec14-F33 | anchor: A16
Light-rail crossings need full track clearance, waiting until gates lift and reds quit, with a flashing train emblem as caution only rather than a stop order [A16].
Why it matters: separates warning emblem from control signal.
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0099]

Misconceptions: bikes may ride against traffic; horns help near bikes; trucks stop like cars; trains can stop fast.
Mnemonics: MIRROR means if you lack the trucker in glass you are unseen; FIFTEEN-FIFTY marks rail halt distance.
Glossary: vulnerable user; bike lane; move-over; no-zone; lane filtering; crossbuck; HOV.
Dynamic: pedestrian death counts and peak months and hours stay year-variable and are not stated as stable rules here.
